description: Julien Sorel, a carpenter's son, wants to rise in a France that is closed to him. Stendhal invents the modern psychological novel.

hero.hook: Red for the uniform, black for the cassock: two colors, one ambition.

blocks.text: Published in **1830**, **The Red and the Black** is the birth certificate of the psychological novel, the novel centered on what a character thinks. **Stendhal**, whose real name was **Henri Beyle**, follows **Julien Sorel**, a young commoner with no title, eaten up by ambition under the **[[French Restoration (1815-1830)]]**, when the Bourbons came back to power after Napoleon.

Between nostalgia for Napoleon and a suffocating society, the novel dissects social hypocrisy and the torments of a soul looking for its place. Julien misses the days when talent could rise through the army. Stendhal shows, with cold clarity, how people calculate their own feelings to get ahead. Julien becomes the model of the modern romantic hero: intelligent, proud, and trapped by his time.

Stendhal claimed a dry style, shaped by his years as a soldier under Napoleon. He called it **[[Beylism]]**: clarity, sincerity, refusal of romantic swelling. For him, writing meant analyzing human passion coldly.

blocks.caption: Stendhal: the pitiless analyst of the passions

blocks.text: Stendhal read a few pages of the Civil Code every morning to keep his tone natural and free of grand effects.

The subtitle, **[[Chronicle of 1830]]**, recalls the book's double ambition: to paint a soul with precision and to draw the portrait of a France gone stiff, frozen and unable to change. The novel appeared shortly before the **Three Glorious Days**, the July 1830 revolution that overthrew Charles X.

The despised son of a carpenter, Julien has a rare intelligence. He can recite the **[[Vulgate]]**, the Latin translation of the Bible, from memory. By **1830** the “red” of the army uniform, the career Napoleon had opened, had given way to the “black” of the cassock, the only road to power for an educated commoner.

blocks.caption: Restoration France: a society where ambition has to hide

blocks.text: Julien enters the seminary, the school for priests, then becomes tutor to the **de Rênal** family at **Verrières**, in Franche-Comté. His conquest of **Madame de Rênal** starts as a military operation, not as love at first sight. Hypocrisy becomes his survival tool. The plot grew out of a real case, that of **Antoine Berthet**, a seminarian sentenced to death in **1827**.

sections.title: Julien Sorel: energy against the system

blocks.text: In Paris, Julien becomes secretary to the **marquis de La Mole**, a great aristocrat. He seduces **Mathilde de La Mole**, a proud young woman who loves danger and scandal. Julien sees her as the final trophy of his climb.

In Stendhal, love is often a performance in which people watch themselves more than they let go. Julien wins a noble title and permission to marry Mathilde, but a letter from **Madame de Rênal** exposes his lies. **[[The symbolism of The Red and the Black]]** sets the army uniform against the priest's cassock, the only two levers of advancement for a commoner in this closed society.

sections.title: From the provinces to the Paris salons

blocks.text: Julien shoots Madame de Rênal in the church at Verrières, after she has written that damning letter. In prison he stops calculating. Facing death, ambition gives way to regret for the happiness he knew with her. He refuses to save his head through intrigue or aristocratic protection. **Mathilde** carries away his severed head in a theatrical gesture, true to her character. Stendhal shows that only the truth of feeling survives the social theater.
